reviews.title: Excellent sound and mic - long cord- great value
reviews.comment: Update:  After 3-4 years this headset has worked great daily but due to all the twisting it now has wire exposed.  Still 5 stars. Still the best cheap headset out there .  Buying another one now After looking at the logitech similar headsets I went with this Sennheiser brand for the quality and having the earpiece on the RIGHT side is great.  I use this when working from home and I can hear everyone and the mic is perfect.  No problems, no static and no feedback.  I just plugged it into my USB port and it installed and worked in less than a minute.  Very lightweight and it has a long cord with a mute button on the cord.  I would say if you want a great headset on the right side ear, get this one.

reviews.title: Solid value for the price
reviews.comment: I bought this headset specifically for use with Skype/Lync calls, as it's designed to be ideal for.  Everything worked as expected, and the sound quality was remarkably good for the cost.  The inline remote functions well for both volume and call control.  It's nearly flawless for use in a quiet office.  I like the one-ear design which is more comfortable for long-term wearing and less isolating.  The true test was when I needed to work from a Starbucks for a few hours before a meeting I had at a remote office.  The quality was good enough for me to speak with customers, and they could hear clearly without excessive background noise.  I had to keep myself muted when not talking, and when they used the blender, I often needed to repeat myself, but still pretty good considering the environment.  The only thing I would have liked is if the headset could be a bit louder for me to hear over the surroundings.  Other headsets I have supply a bit more volume.  Still, a solid value for the price.  Nice to get some equipment from one of the classic pro audio brands.
reviews.author: ChrisNorthJersey

reviews.title: Just magically works
reviews.comment: PROS: * Plugs in and just works without any special drivers. * Works with WebEx, GoToMeeting, Skype, etc * Mute button is in-line, so it works in any app rather than being a programmed hotkey for a specific app. * Volume control is standard PC volume up and down. * Frequency response is good enough for music, games, etc as well. * Can still hear people around me if they need to get my attention. * Very lightweight. CONS: * I should have gotten the ML60 version for stereo. This works for any audio source and shows up as a sound device.  It does not isolate sound, so it's probably better to get the 260 model if you are in a loud callcenter.  If you want it for serious audiophiles or 3d sound, then you want the 660 with bigger earcups.  However, those are going to be heavier.
reviews.author: Josh (Xaminmo) Davis

reviews.title: For me: Good sound, bad control placement
reviews.comment: So close to what I wanted, but I am disappointed. The Good: The sound is great both on the speaker and what people tell me they hear on on the mic.  The headset part also lightweight. The Bad: The headset adjustment is a bit awkward - it only extends on the speaker side, so when fully extended to fit my big head I have a long flat run in the band that doesn't leave it balanced.  But my real problem with this headset is the inline volume control.  First of all, its huge compared to what you would encounter with modern headphones so it weighs the cord down and it hangs at an awkward length along the cord from the headset.  It won't rest on my desk.  It slides off and will get the cord caught under the arm of my chair.  It needs about another foot of slack and I could just fix it to my desk with a command strip and all would be well.  But if I did that with this length, my neck would be arched and it would be like I am on a leash.  I may try clipping it to my shirt at the inline control so that the weight doesn't pull the cord down.
reviews.author: Supertronic
